A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLM-Streamline study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v4 reports original pruning evaluations, stability analyses, ablations, and LoRA comparisons in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those experiments and adds inference-speed measurements, Llama3.1 and Mixtral evaluations, and results at approximately 50% pruning.

M1.justification: Cosine-based contiguous-layer selection, lightweight replacement networks, initialization options, and the MSE training objective remain unchanged. The additional model evaluations do not document a new algorithm or adaptation.

E1.justification: Training data and evaluation tasks remain unchanged, including the classification and generation benchmarks and the smaller-OPT benchmark suite. Llama3.1, Mixtral, and higher pruning ratios expand model configurations rather than represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in matched experiments. The added Llama3.1 and high-pruning comparisons reuse SliceGPT and LLM-Pruner; the Mixtral tables compare existing LLM-Streamline variants and the dense model. No new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: v5 substantially expands model settings to Llama3.1-8B, Llama3.1-70B, and Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1, including approximately 30% pruning for the 70B model. It also adds approximately 50% pruning on Llama2-7B and a throughput evaluation generating sequences of length 128. These are additional protocols; existing experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.7 adds a high-pruning sensitivity test beyond the earlier pruning-ratio analyses, while Appendix D adds a practical inference-speed comparison. Existing network, initialization, data-sensitivity, post-training, and LoRA analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The PPL standard deviations used to quantify answer confidence and construct stability remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched existing results are unchanged, but v5 adds substantial results in Tables 11, 21–24, and 26–27. For example, Ours (Layer) reports 68.8 average accuracy and 90.9 stability on Llama3.1-70B at 30.3% pruning, and 38.5 accuracy and 72.5 stability on Llama2-7B at 48% pruning. These are newly reported settings, not performance improvements over corresponding v4 results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, including the layer-selection objective, replacement loss, confidence calculation, and stability definition, are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same pruning-and-replacement contribution, stability-metric claim, and effectiveness and training-efficiency claims. The introductory 93% classification and 77% generation retention claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 now qualifies the linear performance–parameter relationship as applying at modest pruning ratios. New Appendix D acknowledges slightly slower inference than SliceGPT and LLM-Pruner. The existing limitation concerning quantization is retained, moving from Appendix E to F.

D1.justification: The v5 abstract adds a code-repository hyperlink absent from v4. This supplies new access information, although repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Data-mixture and training implementation disclosures in Appendices B–C remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference lists and Section 5 research positioning are unchanged. The added model evaluations do not introduce identifiable new cited works or revise the claimed distinction from earlier pruning methods.

P1.justification: v5 makes limited wording edits, updates the publication header, inserts an inference-speed appendix, and expands the experimental appendix with corresponding cross-reference updates. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact. Some newly added model citations render as question marks.

P2.justification: v5 adds seven tables using the existing presentation style, moves table captions above their tables, resizes Figure 2, and relocates Figure 4 beside Figure 3 with a shorter caption. Existing plotted results and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The larger-model, MoE, and high-pruning evaluations strengthen empirical support, while the new throughput comparison documents a practical tradeoff absent from v4. The code link and narrower Section 4.6 interpretation also help. These gains outweigh limited reporting defects, including sparse details for the added evaluations and Table 26's inconsistent LLM-Pruner retained performance: its displayed averages imply about 62.4%, rather than the reported 63.4%, without changing the ranking.
